content:
Container Usage The application can run without copying config.yaml into the container. If no config file exists, it will automatically create one with sensible defaults.
Environment Variable Support Soulsolid supports environment variables in configuration files using the !env_var tag:
metadata: providers: discogs: secret: !env_var DISCOGS_API_KEYSecrets can also be loaded from a file (handy for Docker/Kubernetes secrets) with the !env_file tag: the named environment variable holds the path to the file, and the file’s contents become the value. See Configuration for details.
The application will fail to start if a referenced environment variable is not set.
Podman / Docker # Build the image (or use the published contre95/soulsolid image) podman build -t soulsolid . # Create folders mkdir music downloads logs data config # Run with docker/podman podman run -d --name soulsolid -p 3535:3535 \ -v ./music:/app/music \ -v ./downloads:/app/downloads \ -v ./logs:/app/logs \ -v ./data:/data \ -v ./config:/config contre95/soulsolid:latestThe web interface will be available at http://localhost:3535.
The container works from /app, so the generated default config stores the library in /app/music, downloads in /app/downloads and job logs in /app/logs/jobs. The database defaults to /app/library.db; to keep it on the ./data volume, set database.path: /data/library.db in config/config.yaml.
Compose Here’s an example compose.yaml file:
services: soulsolid: image: contre95/soulsolid:latest ports: - "3535:3535" volumes: - ./config:/config - ./data:/data - ./logs:/app/logs - ./music:/app/music - ./downloads:/app/downloads environment: # optional, only if your config.yaml references them - DISCOGS_API_KEY=your_discogs_key_here restart: unless-stoppedPodman kube / Kubernetes Alternatively, you can use Podman-kube pod YAMLs for deployment:
apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: soulsolid labels: app: soulsolid spec: restartPolicy: OnFailure containers: - name: soulsolid image: contre95/soulsolid:latest ports: - containerPort: 3535 hostPort: 3535 volumeMounts: - mountPath: /config/config.yaml name: config - mountPath: /music name: music - mountPath: /downloads name: downloads volumes: - name: music hostPath: path: /path/to/soulsolid_music type: DirectoryOrCreate - name: downloads hostPath: path: /path/to/soulsolid_downloads type: DirectoryOrCreate - name: config hostPath: path: ./config/config.yaml type: FileWhen mounting your own config.yaml, point libraryPath and downloadPath at the mounted directories (/music and /downloads above).
For a Kubernetes Deployment + ConfigMap, see the Kubernetes examples.
Logs Soulsolid logs to the container’s output, so podman logs soulsolid (or docker logs soulsolid) shows what it’s doing. Each background job also writes its own log, by default under /app/logs/jobs, which you can read from the Jobs section of the app. See Logging.
Health check GET /health returns OK while Soulsolid is running, for container health checks or Kubernetes probes. See Hosting.
Development Want to run Soulsolid from source or contribute? See the Development section of the README and the contributing guide.

content:
The Library is the heart of Soulsolid: it’s your music collection once it has been imported. Everything else in the app (importing, downloading, tagging, lyrics) ends up here, and the Library section is where you browse, search, inspect and clean it up.
What you can do Browse every track in the collection, page by page. Search artists, albums and tracks from a single search box. Filter tracks by genre, lyrics, AcoustID or date added. Open a track overview with its tags and audio details. Jump to the tag editor, add to a playlist, or play a track. Delete tracks, albums or whole artists. See collection stats: how many artists, albums and tracks you have and how much disk space they use. Browsing and searching With the search box empty, the Library lists every track in your collection, 50 per page.
Start typing to search. A single query looks at artist names, album titles and track titles at the same time. Matching albums and artists are listed first, followed by matching tracks. A track matches if its title, its artist or its album contains the text you typed.
Filters Filters narrow down the track results and can be combined with each other and with a text search:
Filter What it does Genre Only tracks with exactly that genre. AcoustID Only tracks that have (or don’t have) an AcoustID. Useful to find tracks that still need identifying. Lyrics Has lyrics, Empty lyrics, Instrumental, or Lyrics contain… to search inside the lyrics text. Added after / before Only tracks added to the library in a given date range. Track overview The Overview button opens a floating panel with everything Soulsolid knows about a track: title, artist, album, year, genre, track number, ISRC, BPM and lyrics, plus technical details such as format, bitrate, sample rate, bit depth, channels, duration and the file’s location on disk. You can also play the track right there (see Streaming).
From each search result you can also:
Edit Tags to open the track in the tag editor. Add to Playlist to add the track, or a whole album or artist, to one of your playlists. Deleting music You can delete a single track, an album, or an artist with all their tracks.
Deleting removes the audio files from disk, not just the entry in the library. This can’t be undone.
If a file can’t be removed (for example it was already deleted by hand), the entry is still removed from the library and the problem is logged.
Collection stats The dashboard and the Library show how many artists, albums and tracks you have, and the total size of your library folder on disk.
The folder buttons at the top of the Library open a folder tree of your library or downloads folder in a new tab, so you can check at a glance how files are laid out on disk. This needs the tree command to be installed (it is in the official container image).
Configuration The Library has no settings of its own. It uses:
libraryPath: /app/music # where your organized music lives downloadPath: /app/downloads # shown in the downloads folder tree database: path: /data/library.db # the library databaseRelated Importing and Downloading add music to the library. Metadata and Lyrics enrich the tracks already in it. Merge cleans up duplicate artists, albums, genres and tracks. Metrics turns the library into charts.

The config.yaml file contains all application settings. Key sections:
libraryPath / downloadPath: Where the library lives and where downloads land import: Import settings and file organization rules (see Importing and Paths) metadata: Metadata provider settings (musicbrainz, deezer, discogs, acoustid) lyrics: Lyrics provider settings (see Lyrics) downloaders: External service configurations in the form of plugins. Supports both local .so files and automatic building from Git repositories (see Downloading) jobs: Job logs and webhooks (see Jobs) server, database, logger: Web server port, SQLite path and logging telegram: Bot configuration and allowed users (deprecated, will be removed in v0.30.0) Security Note: Never commit sensitive values like tokens or API keys to version control. Use environment variables or secret files instead.
The config file is read from /config/config.yaml by default; set SOULSOLID_CONFIG_PATH to use another location.
Automatic Configuration If no config.yaml file exists when the application starts, it will automatically create one with sensible default values. This means you can run Soulsolid out of the box without any configuration!
Example Configuration This is the repository’s config.example.yaml:
libraryPath: ./music downloadPath: ./downloads # Deprecated: the Telegram bot will be removed in v0.30.0. telegram: enabled: false # token: !env_var TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN allowedUsers: - <your telegram username> bot_handle: SoulsolidExampleBot # Without the @ logger: enabled: true level: info format: text htmx_debug: false downloaders: plugins: - name: dummy url: https://github.com/contre95/soulsolid-dummy-plugin # path: ../soulsolid-dummy-plugin/plugin.so # Optional if building the plugin icon: https://demo2.contre.io/img/galaxy.png config: {} # Plugin specific config. See https://git.sr.ht/~canuslector/soulsolid-deemix-plugin artwork: embedded: enabled: true size: 1000 quality: 85 server: show_routes: false port: 3535 database: path: ./library.db # Path to the SQLite Database import: move: false # If false tracks will be kepts in the folder where you are importing them from and copied from it to your 'libraryPath:' always_queue: false # When true, it will queue every single imported track for manual review. duplicates: queue # queue | skip | replace allow_missing_metadata: # Per-field: when true the missing value is filled with a fallback default on import, otherwise the track is sent to the manual review queue artist: false album: false title: false year: false genre: false paths: compilations: '%asciify{$albumartist}/%asciify{$album} (%if{$original_year,$original_year,$year})/%asciify{$track $title}' album:soundtrack: '%asciify{$albumartist}/%asciify{$album} [OST] (%if{$original_year,$original_year,$year})/%asciify{$track $title}' album:single: '%asciify{$albumartist}/%asciify{$album} [Single] (%if{$original_year,$original_year,$year})/%asciify{$track $title}' album:ep: '%asciify{$albumartist}/%asciify{$album} [EP] (%if{$original_year,$original_year,$year})/%asciify{$track $title}' default_path: '%asciify{$albumartist}/%asciify{$album} (%if{$original_year,$original_year,$year})/%asciify{$track $title}' auto_start_watcher: false metadata: providers: acoustid: enabled: true # secret: !env_var ACOUSTID_CLIENT_KEY # You can login with Musicbrainz -> https://acoustid.org/new-application # secret: !env_file ACOUSTID_CLIENT_KEY_FILE # Or load it from a file instead, e.g. a Docker secret deezer: enabled: true discogs: enabled: true # secret: !env_var DISCOGS_API_KEY # You can get it here -> https://www.discogs.com/settings/developers # secret: !env_file DISCOGS_API_KEY_FILE # Or load it from a file instead, e.g. a Docker secret musicbrainz: enabled: true lyrics: providers: lrclib: enabled: true prefer_synced: false # Some programs like navidrome require synced lyrics jobs: log: true log_path: ./logs/jobs webhooks: enabled: true job_trigger: - directory_import - download_album command: "echo hi"Environment Variables Any config value can be read from an environment variable with the !env_var tag, or from a file whose path is in an environment variable with the !env_file tag (the Docker/Kubernetes secrets convention). The application fails to start if a referenced variable is not set, or if the file can’t be read or is empty.
metadata: providers: discogs: secret: !env_var DISCOGS_API_KEY acoustid: secret: !env_file ACOUSTID_CLIENT_KEY_FILE # e.g. ACOUSTID_CLIENT_KEY_FILE=/run/secrets/acoustid_client_keyThe variable names in the examples above are conventions, not fixed names. The app itself reads:
Variable Description Default SOULSOLID_CONFIG_PATH Path to the config file /config/config.yaml IMAGE_TAG Application version shown in the UI dev

content:
The Download section lets you search external music services and download tracks, albums, whole artists and playlists. Soulsolid doesn’t come with any music service built in: each service is added through a downloader plugin, so what you can search and download depends on the plugins you have configured. See Downloading for how to install one.
Downloaded music lands in your download folder, not straight in the library. From there it is imported, either by hand or automatically with the download folder watcher, and organized into your library.
What you can do Search a service for albums, artists or tracks. Paste a link to a track, album, playlist or artist from the service. Browse an album’s track list or an artist’s albums before downloading. See the service’s charts (top tracks), if the plugin supports it. Download a single track, a full album, an artist’s whole discography, a selection of tracks, or a playlist. Check whether your account and credentials for the service are working. Choosing a service Each configured plugin appears under Downloaders in the sidebar, with its icon. Click one to open the Download section for that service. The first plugin in your configuration is the default.
Not every service supports everything. Each plugin tells Soulsolid what it can do (searching, searching artists, pasting links, charts), and the Download section only shows the options the selected service supports.
Account status The service panel shows who you’re logged in as and the state of your credentials:
Status Meaning Valid Everything is working. Invalid credentials Your login or API key was rejected or has expired. Update it in the plugin’s config and restart. Disabled The plugin is loaded but not active. If no plugin is configured, the Download section tells you so and links to the setup instructions.
Searching Type in the search box and pick what you’re looking for: Albums, Artists, Tracks or Link. Searches return 20 results by default.
With Link, paste a URL from the music service. Soulsolid works out whether it points to a track, an album, a playlist or an artist and shows the matching result, ready to download.
Downloading Downloads run in the background as jobs, so you can keep using the app while they run. Starting a download shows a confirmation, and you can follow its progress (and read its log) in the Jobs section.
Each downloaded file is:
Tagged with the metadata provided by the service (title, artists, album, year, genre, track and disc number, ISRC and more). Given cover art, embedded in the file if artwork embedding is enabled. Saved with a safe filename, with characters that aren’t allowed on disk removed. When a download finishes, the files are in your download folder waiting to be imported.
Configuration downloadPath: /app/downloads # where downloaded files are saved downloaders: plugins: - name: dummy url: https://github.com/contre95/soulsolid-dummy-plugin # build from git, or # path: /app/plugins/dummy/plugin.so # use a pre-built plugin icon: https://demo2.contre.io/img/galaxy.png # shown in the UI config: {} # settings for the plugin itself, e.g. API keys artwork: embedded: enabled: true # embed cover art into downloaded files size: 1000 # maximum artwork size in pixels quality: 85 # JPEG quality (0-100)See Downloading for installing plugins.
Related Downloading setup: installing and configuring plugins. Importing: moves downloaded files into the library. Jobs: follow and cancel running downloads. Plugins: writing your own downloader plugin.

content:
Importing is how music gets into your library. Point Soulsolid at a folder and it reads each file’s tags, checks whether you already have the song, organizes the file into your library folder and adds it to the library. Anything that needs your decision, such as a duplicate or a track with missing tags, is held in a review queue instead of being imported blindly.
This page explains how importing works from the app. For every import setting (duplicate policy, path templates, FAT32 options) see the Importing configuration guide and Paths.
What you can do Import a folder, including all its subfolders. Let Soulsolid watch your download folder and import new music automatically. Review queued tracks: duplicates, tracks with missing tags, and failed imports. Act on the queue one track at a time or a whole artist or album at once. Clean up the download folder once you’re done. Importing a folder In the Import section, enter the folder to import (it defaults to your download folder) and start the import. It runs in the background as a job, so you can follow its progress and log in the Jobs section.
Only MP3 and FLAC files are imported; anything else in the folder is ignored.
For each file, Soulsolid:
Reads its tags and computes an audio fingerprint. Checks for duplicates: is the same recording already in your library? Checks for missing tags: does it have an artist, album, title, year and genre? Either imports it or sends it to the review queue. When a track is imported, its file is copied (or moved, if you enabled Move files instead of copying) into your library folder, at a location built from your path templates. Artists and albums are created automatically.
When the job finishes it reports how many tracks, albums and artists were imported, and how many were skipped, queued or failed.
Re-importing Importing the same folder twice is safe. Tracks already in the library at the same location are skipped, and a track that was imported before from somewhere else is updated in place instead of being added a second time.
Watching the download folder Turn on Watch Mode in the Import section to have Soulsolid watch your download folder. When a new file appears there, Soulsolid waits for any running job to finish (for example, the download that’s still writing files) and then imports the download folder automatically.
To have the watcher start every time Soulsolid starts, set import.auto_start_watcher: true.
The review queue The review queue holds tracks that need your decision. A track can be in the queue for more than one reason at once, and each reason is shown as a badge on it:
Reason Why it’s queued What you can do Manual review You enabled Always queue tracks for review. Import, Cancel, Delete Duplicate The same recording is already in your library. Replace, Skip, Delete Missing metadata A required tag is missing (see Allow missing metadata). Cancel, Delete Failed import Something went wrong importing it, e.g. the file couldn’t be read. Skip, Delete What each action does:
Import: adds the track to the library. Replace: replaces the copy already in your library with this file. The existing library entry is kept and updated, so it stays in your playlists. Cancel / Skip: removes the track from the queue and leaves the file where it is. Delete: removes the track from the queue and deletes the file from disk. You can play a queued track and see its cover art right from the queue to help you decide.
Missing tags block the library. While a track is missing a required tag, Import and Replace are disabled, so an incomplete track can never be added to your library or overwrite one that’s already there. Fix its tags in the tag editor first.
Grouping and bulk actions Use the buttons at the top of the queue to switch between the individual view and grouping by artist or by album. In a group you can apply an action to every track at once. Bulk actions only touch the tracks they make sense for: Import skips duplicates (use Replace for those), and Replace only touches duplicates.
Clear Queue empties the whole queue.
The queue is kept in memory, so it’s emptied when Soulsolid restarts. The files themselves are not touched; import the folder again to queue them again.
Cleaning up the download folder After importing, Prune Download Path (in the Import section) deletes the MP3 and FLAC files left in your download folder and clears the review queue. Use it when you’ve finished reviewing and want to start fresh.
Configuration import: move: false # copy files into the library (false) or move them (true) always_queue: false # send every track to the review queue duplicates: queue # queue | skip | replace allow_missing_metadata: # per tag: true = fill in a default, false = send to the queue artist: false album: false title: false year: false genre: false auto_start_watcher: false paths: default_path: '%asciify{$albumartist}/%asciify{$album}/%asciify{$track $title}' fat32_safe: false downloadPath: /app/downloads # the folder that's watched and prunedAll of these can also be changed from the Settings page. See the Importing configuration guide for what each option does.
Related Importing configuration and Paths: every import option and the path template syntax. Metadata: fix missing tags before importing a queued track. Downloading: produces the files the watcher picks up. Jobs: follow and cancel imports.

content:
Path templates decide where each track is placed in your library folder, based on its tags. This page describes the placeholders and functions you can use in them. Templates are used both when importing and when reorganizing your library.
Placeholders Placeholders are variables that get replaced with actual metadata values from the track. They are prefixed with a $ symbol.
Available Placeholders Placeholder Description Data Type Example Value $albumartist The name of the first album artist String “The Beatles” $album The album title String “Abbey Road” $year The release year Integer “1969” $original_year The original release year (if different from release year) Integer “1969” $track The track number, zero-padded to 2 digits String “01” $title The track title String “Come Together” $format Audio format of the file String “flac” $genre Music genre String “Rock” Functions Functions perform operations on placeholders or other values. They are prefixed with % and use curly braces for arguments.
Available Functions artistfolder Groups tracks into letter-based subfolders by artist name, similar to how music stores organize physical media. The value is first asciified, then prefixed with its uppercase first letter (A–Z) or # for non-alphabetic names.
Syntax: %artistfolder{value}
Parameters:
value: Any string value or placeholder (typically $albumartist) Examples:
%artistfolder{$albumartist}“The Beatles” → T/The Beatles “Björk” → B/Bjork “2Pac” → #/2Pac A typical path using %artistfolder:
%artistfolder{$albumartist}/%asciify{$album} (%if{$original_year,$original_year,$year})/%asciify{$track $title}Result: T/The Beatles/Abbey Road (1969)/01 Come Together
asciify Converts text to ASCII by removing accents, diacritics, and special characters.
Syntax: %asciify{value}
Parameters:
value: Any string value or placeholder Example:
%asciify{$albumartist}For “Björk” → “Bjork”
if Conditional rendering that returns one of two values based on a condition.
Syntax: %if{condition,true_value,false_value}
Parameters:
condition: Expression to evaluate (returns true if not empty, “0”, or “false”) true_value: Value to return if condition is true false_value: Value to return if condition is false (optional) Examples:
%if{$original_year,$original_year,$year}Returns $original_year if it exists, otherwise $year
%if{$albumartist,$albumartist,Various Artists}Returns $albumartist if it exists, otherwise “Various Artists”
Usage Examples Basic Path Template $albumartist/$album ($year)/$track $titleResult: The Beatles/Abbey Road (1969)/01 Come Together
With ASCII Conversion %asciify{$albumartist}/%asciify{$album} (%if{$original_year,$original_year,$year})/%asciify{$track $title}Result: The Beatles/Abbey Road (1969)/01 Come Together
Album Type Specific Paths Default Album %asciify{$albumartist}/%asciify{$album} (%if{$original_year,$original_year,$year})/%asciify{$track $title}EP %asciify{$albumartist}/%asciify{$album} [EP] (%if{$original_year,$original_year,$year})/%asciify{$track $title}Single %asciify{$albumartist}/%asciify{$album} [Single] (%if{$original_year,$original_year,$year})/%asciify{$track $title}Soundtrack %asciify{$albumartist}/%asciify{$album} [OST] (%if{$original_year,$original_year,$year})/%asciify{$track $title}Compilation %asciify{$albumartist}/%asciify{$album} (%if{$original_year,$original_year,$year})/%asciify{$track $title}Advanced Examples Conditional Album Artist %if{$albumartist,%asciify{$albumartist},Various Artists}/%asciify{$album} (%if{$original_year,$original_year,$year})/%asciify{$track $title}Year with Fallback %asciify{$albumartist}/%asciify{$album} (%if{$original_year,$original_year,%if{$year,$year,Unknown}})/%asciify{$track $title}Notes All placeholders are replaced with actual metadata values from the track Functions can be nested within each other Unknown placeholders are left as-is in the output The %asciify function is particularly useful for creating filesystem-safe paths The %if function allows for conditional logic in path templates Track numbers are automatically zero-padded to 2 digits Years are converted to strings automatically Configuration These templates can be configured in the config.yaml file under the import.paths section:
import: paths: default_path: '%asciify{$albumartist}/%asciify{$album} (%if{$original_year,$original_year,$year})/%asciify{$track $title}' album:ep: '%asciify{$albumartist}/%asciify{$album} [EP] (%if{$original_year,$original_year,$year})/%asciify{$track $title}' album:single: '%asciify{$albumartist}/%asciify{$album} [Single] (%if{$original_year,$original_year,$year})/%asciify{$track $title}' album:soundtrack: '%asciify{$albumartist}/%asciify{$album} [OST] (%if{$original_year,$original_year,$year})/%asciify{$track $title}' compilations: '%asciify{$albumartist}/%asciify{$album} (%if{$original_year,$original_year,$year})/%asciify{$track $title}'Reorganize Library The Reorganize feature applies the current path templates to every track in the library and physically moves files to match. It is useful after changing path templates or after bulk metadata corrections.
How It Works Start it from Analyze → File Paths. For every track in your library, Soulsolid:
Works out where the track should be, using your current path templates Skips it if its file is missing from disk Skips it if it’s already in the right place Otherwise moves the file to its new location, creating folders as needed, and updates the library Removes folders left empty after files were moved out It runs as a background job that you can follow in the Jobs section. When it finishes, it reports how many files were moved, skipped and failed. See Reorganize for more.
FAT32 Safe Mode FAT32 safe mode makes every folder and file name FAT32-compatible:
Everything is lowercased, so names don’t clash when syncing to FAT32 (where Rock/ and rock/ are the same folder) Characters FAT32 doesn’t allow (: * ? " < > | \) are replaced with - Trailing dots and spaces are removed Names longer than 255 bytes are shortened, keeping the file extension When two tracks would end up at the same path, a number (_1, _2, …) is added so both files are kept This is useful when you sync your library to a FAT32 drive (e.g. an SD card, a USB stick or some NAS setups), while the library itself stays on a normal filesystem.
During Import Enable it with import.paths.fat32_safe: true in the config, or the FAT32-safe filenames checkbox in Settings. Every imported file then gets a FAT32-safe path.
During Reorganize Analyze → File Paths has its own FAT32-safe filenames checkbox that applies only to that run, useful for a one-off cleanup when the setting is off.
summary: Path templates decide where each track is placed in your library folder, based on its tags. This page describes the placeholders and functions you can use in them. Templates are used both when importing and when reorganizing your library.
title: Paths

content:
Soulsolid imports music from folders on the server. When importing, it reads each file’s tags, checks whether you already have the song, moves or copies the file into your library folder, and creates artists and albums as needed.
This page covers the import settings. For how to import and review tracks in the app, see Importing.
Configuration Options Import behavior is controlled in config.yaml (most options can also be changed from the Settings page):
import: move: false # if false, files are copied; if true, originals are removed after import always_queue: false # queue every track for manual review, even non-duplicates duplicates: queue # queue | skip | replace allow_missing_metadata: # per-field control over importing tracks with missing metadata artist: false # when true, a missing field is filled with a fallback default on import; album: false # when false, a track missing that field is sent to the missing_metadata queue title: false year: false genre: false auto_start_watcher: false # automatically watch the download path on startup paths: compilations: '%asciify{$genre}/%asciify{$format}/%asciify{$albumartist}/%asciify{$album} (%if{$original_year,$original_year,$year})/%asciify{$track $title}' album:soundtrack: '%asciify{$genre}/%asciify{$format}/%asciify{$albumartist}/%asciify{$album} [OST] (%if{$original_year,$original_year,$year})/%asciify{$track $title}' album:single: '%asciify{$genre}/%asciify{$format}/%asciify{$albumartist}/%asciify{$album} [Single] (%if{$original_year,$original_year,$year})/%asciify{$track $title}' album:ep: '%asciify{$genre}/%asciify{$format}/%asciify{$albumartist}/%asciify{$album} [EP] (%if{$original_year,$original_year,$year})/%asciify{$track $title}' default_path: '%asciify{$genre}/%asciify{$format}/%asciify{$albumartist}/%asciify{$album} (%if{$original_year,$original_year,$year})/%asciify{$track $title}' fat32_safe: false # lowercase paths, strip FAT32-forbidden characters, 255-byte segment limitImport Sources Directory Import Imports every supported audio file in a folder and its subfolders. This is the most common way to bring an existing music collection into Soulsolid.
Supported file formats:
MP3 (.mp3) FLAC (.flac) Process:
Finds every supported audio file in the folder and its subfolders Reads the tags of each file Computes an audio fingerprint to detect duplicates Copies or moves the file into your library folder Creates artists and albums as needed Adds the track to your library Download Path Watcher The watcher keeps an eye on your downloadPath folder. When a new audio file appears there, it waits for any running job to finish (up to 5 minutes, so a download can finish writing its files) and then imports the download folder automatically.
Start it automatically with Soulsolid: import.auto_start_watcher: true Turn it on or off at any time with Watch Mode in the Import section Only new files start an import; changing or deleting files doesn’t File Organization Move vs Copy The import behavior can be configured to either move or copy files:
Move: Files are moved from their original location to the library structure Copy: Files are copied, leaving originals in place Library Structure Files are organized into folders according to your import.paths templates. The following config:
paths: default_path: '%asciify{$albumartist}/%asciify{$album} (%if{$original_year,$original_year,$year})/%asciify{$track $title}'Will produce the following files structure:
Library/ ├── Artist Name/ │ ├── Album Title (Year)/ │ │ ├── 01 - Track Title.mp3 │ │ ├── 02 - Track Title.mp3 │ │ └── ... │ └── ... └── Various Artists/ └── Compilation Album (Year)/ └── ...Special Handling Compilations: Multi-artist albums are placed under Various Artists Path Customization: Different path patterns for singles, EPs, soundtracks, etc. See Paths for examples. Filename Sanitization: Characters that aren’t allowed in file names are removed FAT32-Safe Filenames When fat32_safe: true is set, every folder and file name is made FAT32-compatible on import:
Everything is lowercased, so names don’t clash when syncing to FAT32 (where Rock/ and rock/ are the same folder) Characters FAT32 doesn’t allow (: * ? " < > | \) are replaced with - Trailing dots and spaces are removed Names longer than 255 bytes are shortened, keeping the file extension If two tracks would resolve to the same lowercased path (e.g. Wos/lala.mp3 and WoS/lala.mp3), a number is added to the second (wos/lala_1.mp3) so both files are kept.
Duplicate Detection Duplicates are detected with Chromaprint audio fingerprints, which identify the same recording by how it sounds, regardless of its file name or tags.
To find duplicates already in your library, see Merge.
Duplicate Handling Strategies When duplicates are detected, the system can be configured to:
Skip Ignores duplicate tracks completely No changes made to existing tracks Fastest option for large imports Replace Replaces the track in your library with the new file Updates its tags and location Keeps the existing library entry, so it stays in your playlists A new file that’s missing required tags is queued instead, so it can’t overwrite a complete track Queue Adds duplicate to manual review queue Allows user to decide how to handle each case Most conservative approach Always Queue You can also send every track to the queue, duplicate or not, with always_queue: true.
Forces all tracks (including non-duplicates) into queue Maximum control over import process Useful for carefully curated libraries Import Queue The import queue holds tracks that need your approval before they’re added to the library. The queue is kept in memory, so it’s emptied when Soulsolid restarts (the files themselves aren’t touched).
Queue Types A track can be in the queue for more than one reason at once (e.g. it’s both a duplicate and missing metadata). Each reason is shown as its own badge.
Type Trigger Available Actions Manual review always_queue: true Import, Cancel, Delete Missing metadata Track is missing a tag whose allow_missing_metadata.<field> is false Cancel, Delete Duplicate The same recording is already in your library Replace, Skip, Delete Failed import Something went wrong importing it (e.g. the file can’t be read) Skip, Delete Missing metadata blocks the library. While a track is missing a required tag, Import and Replace are disabled (only Cancel/Skip and Delete remain), so an incomplete track can never be added to your library or overwrite one that’s already there. For example, a duplicate that’s also missing metadata can only be skipped or deleted until its tags are fixed in the tag editor.
See Importing → The review queue for what each action does.
Telegram Integration Deprecated: the Telegram bot will be removed in v0.30.0. Use the web UI instead.
You can interact with the import queue directly from Telegram using the following commands:
/queue - Show the current queue and process items one by one /queue_clear - Clear the entire import queue When using /queue, you’ll receive queue items with inline buttons to:
Import or Cancel for manual review items Replace or Skip for duplicate items Next to proceed to the next item Cancel Session to end the current queue session This allows you to manage imports remotely without needing to access the web interface.
Queue Behavior with Move Option With move: true, a queued track is removed from the queue once it’s imported, since its original file has been moved into your library and is no longer where the queue expects it.
Import Statistics Each import job reports:
Imported: tracks, albums and artists added to the library Skipped: duplicates that were ignored Queued: tracks sent to the review queue Errors: tracks that failed, with details in the job log
summary: Soulsolid imports music from folders on the server. When importing, it reads each file’s tags, checks whether you already have the song, moves or copies the file into your library folder, and creates artists and albums as needed.

The tag editor is where you view and fix a track’s tags. You can edit them by hand, or pull metadata from online providers (MusicBrainz, Discogs and Deezer) and review it before saving. Soulsolid can also identify tracks by how they sound using AcoustID, either one track at a time or for your whole library.
What you can do View and edit a track’s tags. Fetch metadata from MusicBrainz, Discogs or Deezer, or search them and pick the right match. Mark a track as instrumental. Fingerprint a track and look up its AcoustID. Run an AcoustID analysis over the whole library. The tag editor Open the tag editor from the Edit Tags button on any track in the Library, from the import queue, or from a failed track in a job log.
The editor shows the tags as they are in the audio file right now, so what you see is what’s actually on disk. You can edit:
Title and version (remix, live version, …) Artists and album artist Album, year and genre Track number and disc number ISRC, composer, BPM and replay gain Lyrics Artists and albums are picked from the ones already in your library. The editor also shows the cover art embedded in the file and lets you play or download the track.
Click Save Changes to write your changes both to the audio file and to the library.
Instrumental tracks Check Instrumental for tracks that have no lyrics. This clears any lyrics and tells Soulsolid to skip the track when fetching lyrics, so it won’t keep showing up as “lyrics not found”.
Getting metadata from providers The provider buttons at the top of the editor (MusicBrainz, Discogs, Deezer) search that service using the track’s current artist, album, title and year. Only providers enabled in your configuration are shown.
The results appear in a list showing each match’s artist, album, year, genre and ISRC. Pick the right one and the form is filled in with its data. Information that belongs to the file itself (like its audio properties) is kept. If the match comes with an artist or album that isn’t in your library yet, it’s created for you.
Fields filled in by a provider are highlighted in that provider’s color, so you can see where each value came from. Nothing is saved until you click Save Changes, so you can review or adjust the values first.
AcoustID AcoustID identifies recordings by their sound rather than their tags. Soulsolid computes an audio fingerprint of the file (using Chromaprint) and looks it up in the AcoustID database. This is useful for files with wrong or missing tags, and it’s what the Merge section uses to find duplicate tracks.
From the tag editor, the AcoustID button fingerprints the current track and stores its AcoustID. You can also view the stored fingerprint.
AcoustID lookups need a free client key: create an application at acoustid.org/new-application and add it to your configuration (see below).
AcoustID analysis To identify the whole library at once, go to Analyze → Metadata and start an AcoustID Analysis. It runs in the background as a job and:
fingerprints and looks up every track in the library, skips tracks that already have an AcoustID, reports how many tracks were processed, and how many AcoustIDs and fingerprints were added. You can cancel it at any time from the Jobs section. Afterwards, use the AcoustID filter in the Library to find tracks that still couldn’t be identified.
Configuration metadata: providers: acoustid: enabled: true # secret: !env_var ACOUSTID_CLIENT_KEY # your acoustid.org application key deezer: enabled: true discogs: enabled: true # secret: !env_var DISCOGS_API_KEY # https://www.discogs.com/settings/developers musicbrainz: enabled: trueA disabled provider doesn’t show up in the tag editor. See Configuration for keeping keys out of your config file.
Related Lyrics: fetching lyrics from the tag editor or for the whole library. Importing: fix missing tags on queued tracks here. Merge: find duplicates once your tracks have AcoustIDs. Reorganize: move files to match their corrected tags.
summary: The tag editor is where you view and fix a track’s tags. You can edit them by hand, or pull metadata from online providers (MusicBrainz, Discogs and Deezer) and review it before saving. Soulsolid can also identify tracks by how they sound using AcoustID, either one track at a time or for your whole library.
title: Metadata / Tagging

Soulsolid can download music from online music services through downloader plugins. Soulsolid itself isn’t tied to any service: each service is supported by its own plugin, which you add to your configuration. Anyone can write a plugin for a new service (see the Plugin Development Guide).
This page covers installing and configuring plugins. For searching and downloading in the app, see Downloading.
Downloaded tracks are tagged with metadata and land in the configured downloadPath, from where they can be imported into the library.
Installing Plugins Plugins are loaded when Soulsolid starts. There are two ways to install one: let Soulsolid build it from its Git repository on startup (the easiest), or build it into your own container image.
Building a Plugin into the Image You can extend the Soulsolid image to include a plugin. This is the repository’s Containerfile.plugin:
FROM contre95/soulsolid:beta RUN git clone https://github.com/contre95/soulsolid-dummy-plugin /tmp/plugin WORKDIR /tmp/plugin RUN go mod edit -replace=github.com/contre95/soulsolid=/app RUN go mod tidy RUN go build -buildmode=plugin -o /app/plugins/dummy/plugin.so . WORKDIR /appThis downloads the plugin’s source, builds it against the Soulsolid version in the image and places it in /app/plugins/dummy/plugin.so. Point the plugin’s path at that file. Building into the image means Soulsolid starts faster and doesn’t need network access to load the plugin.
Building from a Git Repository Set the plugin’s url to its Git repository instead of a path, and Soulsolid downloads, builds and loads it every time it starts. This needs git and go to be installed, which they are in the official image. Only the repository’s default branch is used. See Building from Git Repositories for details.
Configuration Plugins are configured under the downloaders section:
downloaders: plugins: - name: dummy url: https://github.com/contre95/soulsolid-dummy-plugin # build from git... # path: /app/plugins/dummy/plugin.so # ...or load a pre-built .so icon: https://soulsolid-demo.contre.io/img/galaxy.png config: {} # plugin specific settings, e.g. api keys artwork: embedded: enabled: true size: 1000 # max dimension in pixels quality: 85 # JPEG quality (0-100)For a complete configuration example, see the Configuration documentation.
Downloading Process The details depend on the plugin, but a download generally goes like this:
Login: the plugin logs in to the music service with the credentials in its config Track information: it fetches the track or album details from the service Audio: it downloads the audio Saving: the file is saved to your downloadPath, tagged and with its cover art Downloads run as background jobs. Once done, import them into your library, or turn on the download folder watcher to do it automatically.
Tagging Process After downloading, Soulsolid writes the track’s details into the audio file’s tags:
For MP3 files (ID3v2 tags): Title, Artist, Album, Year, Genre Track/Position in set, Disc number ISRC, BPM, ReplayGain Album art (downloaded from the service) Publisher, Barcode, Composer, Lyrics For FLAC files (Vorbis comments): Similar metadata fields as MP3 Additional Vorbis-specific fields like VERSION, DISCNUMBER
summary: Soulsolid can download music from online music services through downloader plugins. Soulsolid itself isn’t tied to any service: each service is supported by its own plugin, which you add to your configuration. Anyone can write a plugin for a new service (see the Plugin Development Guide).
title: Downloading

Soulsolid can find lyrics for your tracks and save them into the audio files, so any player that reads embedded lyrics can show them. You can fetch lyrics for one track from the tag editor, or run a lyrics analysis over your whole library. Because lyrics you’ve curated by hand are easy to lose, Soulsolid never overwrites existing lyrics without asking: anything unclear goes to a review queue.
Lyrics come from lyrics providers. Currently LRCLIB is supported, which offers both plain and synced (time-stamped) lyrics. See Lyrics configuration for provider settings.
What you can do Fetch lyrics for a single track in the tag editor. Analyze the whole library and add lyrics to every track that’s missing them. Review tracks where the new lyrics differ from the existing ones, or where no lyrics were found. Mark tracks as instrumental so they’re skipped from now on. Lyrics for one track In the tag editor, the Lyrics buttons fetch lyrics from each enabled provider and put them in the lyrics field. Review them and click Save Changes to write them to the file.
Lyrics analysis Go to Analyze → Lyrics, choose a provider and click Start Lyrics Analysis. It runs in the background as a job that goes through every track in your library. You can follow its progress and cancel it from the Jobs section.
Two options control what happens to tracks that already have lyrics (you can pick one or neither):
Option Behavior Skip tracks that already have lyrics (on by default) Tracks with lyrics are left alone; only tracks without lyrics are looked up. Override without queuing New lyrics replace existing ones straight away, without asking. Neither When the new lyrics differ from the existing ones, the track goes to the review queue so you can decide. For every track:
Instrumental tracks are skipped. If the track has no lyrics, the ones found are saved directly. If the new lyrics are identical to the existing ones, nothing changes. If no lyrics are found, or the provider fails, the track goes to the review queue. A track that fails never stops the analysis. When it finishes, the job reports how many tracks were updated, skipped, queued or failed. In the job log, each failed track has a link to open it in the tag editor and fix it by hand.
The lyrics queue The lyrics queue, under Analyze → Lyrics, holds the tracks that need your decision:
Reason What happened What you can do Existing lyrics New lyrics were found that differ from the ones already on the track. Compare the old and new versions. Override with the new lyrics, or Edit Manually Not found The provider has no lyrics for this track. No Lyrics (mark as instrumental), or Edit Manually Failed The provider returned an error. Skip, No Lyrics, or Edit Manually Edit Manually opens the track in the tag editor, where you can paste or fetch lyrics yourself.
As with the import queue, you can group items by artist or by album and act on a whole group at once, or clear the queue.
The lyrics queue is kept in memory, so it’s emptied when Soulsolid restarts. Run the analysis again to rebuild it.
Where lyrics are saved Lyrics are written to the audio file’s tags and to the library, so you can search inside lyrics and see them in the track overview.
Configuration lyrics: providers: lrclib: enabled: true prefer_synced: false # prefer time-stamped lyrics when availableSee Lyrics configuration for details.
Related Lyrics configuration: providers and their options. Metadata / Tagging: the tag editor, and marking tracks as instrumental. Jobs: follow and cancel the lyrics analysis. Library: filter tracks by lyrics.

You can fetch lyrics for one track from the tag editor, or run a lyrics analysis over your whole library. Because lyrics you’ve curated by hand are easy to lose, Soulsolid never overwrites existing lyrics without asking: anything unclear goes to a review queue.

This guide is for developers who want to write a downloader plugin for Soulsolid in Go. If you just want to use an existing plugin, see Downloading instead; no code needed.
Overview Soulsolid supports pluggable downloaders that can be loaded from .so files at runtime. This allows developers to create their own downloaders in separate repositories and distribute them independently.
Plugin Interface Your plugin must implement the Downloader interface:
type Downloader interface { // Search methods SearchAlbums(query string, limit int) ([]music.Album, error) SearchTracks(query string, limit int) ([]music.Track, error) SearchArtists(query string, limit int) ([]music.Artist, error) SearchLinks(query string, limit int) (*LinkResult, error) // Navigation methods GetAlbumTracks(albumID string) ([]music.Track, error) GetArtistAlbums(artistID string) ([]music.Album, error) GetChartTracks(limit int) ([]music.Track, error) // Download methods DownloadTrack(trackID string, downloadDir string, progressCallback func(downloaded, total int64)) (*music.Track, error) DownloadAlbum(albumID string, downloadDir string, progressCallback func(downloaded, total int64)) ([]*music.Track, error) DownloadArtist(artistID string, downloadDir string, progressCallback func(downloaded, total int64)) ([]*music.Track, error) DownloadLink(url string, downloadDir string, progressCallback func(downloaded, total int64)) ([]*music.Track, error) // User info GetUserInfo() *UserInfo GetStatus() DownloaderStatus Name() string Capabilities() DownloaderCapabilities }DownloaderCapabilities tells Soulsolid which UI features to expose for your plugin:
type DownloaderCapabilities struct { SupportsSearch bool // track/album search SupportsArtistSearch bool // artist search SupportsDirectLinks bool // URL/link input SupportsChartTracks bool // charts section }Return downloading.ErrMethodNotSupported from any method your plugin does not implement.
Creating a Plugin Create a new Go module for your plugin: mkdir my-downloader-plugin cd my-downloader-plugin go mod init github.com/yourusername/my-downloader-pluginAdd Soulsolid as a dependency: go get github.com/contre95/soulsolid/src/music go get github.com/contre95/soulsolid/src/features/downloadingImplement your downloader: package main import ( "github.com/contre95/soulsolid/src/features/downloading" "github.com/contre95/soulsolid/src/music" ) type MyDownloader struct { // Your configuration fields apiKey string baseURL string } // Implement the Downloader interface func (d *MyDownloader) Name() string { return "MyDownloader" } func (d *MyDownloader) SearchAlbums(query string, limit int) ([]music.Album, error) { // Implement album search return nil, downloading.ErrMethodNotSupported } func (d *MyDownloader) SearchTracks(query string, limit int) ([]music.Track, error) { // Implement track search return nil, downloading.ErrMethodNotSupported } func (d *MyDownloader) SearchArtists(query string, limit int) ([]music.Artist, error) { return nil, downloading.ErrMethodNotSupported } func (d *MyDownloader) SearchLinks(query string, limit int) (*downloading.LinkResult, error) { return nil, downloading.ErrMethodNotSupported } func (d *MyDownloader) GetAlbumTracks(albumID string) ([]music.Track, error) { return nil, downloading.ErrMethodNotSupported } func (d *MyDownloader) GetArtistAlbums(artistID string) ([]music.Album, error) { return nil, downloading.ErrMethodNotSupported } func (d *MyDownloader) GetChartTracks(limit int) ([]music.Track, error) { return nil, downloading.ErrMethodNotSupported } func (d *MyDownloader) DownloadTrack(trackID string, downloadDir string, progressCallback func(downloaded, total int64)) (*music.Track, error) { // Implement track download return nil, downloading.ErrMethodNotSupported } func (d *MyDownloader) DownloadAlbum(albumID string, downloadDir string, progressCallback func(downloaded, total int64)) ([]*music.Track, error) { return nil, downloading.ErrMethodNotSupported } func (d *MyDownloader) DownloadArtist(artistID string, downloadDir string, progressCallback func(downloaded, total int64)) ([]*music.Track, error) { return nil, downloading.ErrMethodNotSupported } func (d *MyDownloader) DownloadLink(url string, downloadDir string, progressCallback func(downloaded, total int64)) ([]*music.Track, error) { return nil, downloading.ErrMethodNotSupported } func (d *MyDownloader) GetUserInfo() *downloading.UserInfo { return &downloading.UserInfo{Name: "MyDownloader User"} } func (d *MyDownloader) GetStatus() downloading.DownloaderStatus { return downloading.DownloaderStatus{Connected: true} } func (d *MyDownloader) Capabilities() downloading.DownloaderCapabilities { return downloading.DownloaderCapabilities{ SupportsSearch: true, } } // Export the NewDownloader function (this is required!) func NewDownloader(config map[string]interface{}) (downloading.Downloader, error) { apiKey, ok := config["api_key"].(string) if !ok { return nil, fmt.Errorf("api_key is required") } baseURL, ok := config["base_url"].(string) if !ok { baseURL = "https://api.example.com" // default } return &MyDownloader{ apiKey: apiKey, baseURL: baseURL, }, nil }Build the plugin: go build -buildmode=plugin -o mydownloader.so .Configuration Plugins receive their configuration through the NewDownloader function as a map[string]interface{}. The configuration comes from the Soulsolid config file.
Each plugin can optionally specify an icon path for display in the UI.
Example config.yaml:
downloaders: plugins: - name: "mydownloader" # Either specify a URL to build from git: url: "https://github.com/user/soulsolid-myplugin.git" # Or specify a path to a pre-built .so file: # path: "/path/to/mydownloader.so" icon: "path/to/icon.png" # Optional icon for the downloader config: api_key: "your_api_key_here" base_url: "https://api.example.com" timeout: 30Distribution There are two ways to distribute plugins:
Option 1: Pre-built .so files Build for the target platform: Make sure to build the plugin for the same OS and architecture as the Soulsolid binary. Distribute the .so file: Users can place the .so file anywhere accessible to Soulsolid and configure the path in their config. Option 2: Git repositories Publish your plugin source code in a public git repository with a valid go.mod file. Users configure the repository URL in their Soulsolid config (see “Building from Git Repositories” section below). Version compatibility Plugins should be built against the same version of Soulsolid to ensure API compatibility.
Building from Git Repositories Soulsolid can automatically build plugins directly from git repositories. Instead of distributing pre-built .so files, you can specify a repository URL in your configuration.
Configuration Example downloaders: plugins: - name: "mydownloader" url: "https://github.com/user/soulsolid-myplugin.git" # path: "/fallback.so" # Optional fallback path if URL building fails config: api_key: "your_api_key_here"Requirements git must be installed and available in PATH go must be installed (same version as the main application) and available in PATH Network access to clone the repository How It Works Soulsolid clones the repository (default branch only, depth=1) Adds a replace directive to use the local soulsolid module Runs go mod tidy to resolve dependencies Builds the plugin with go build -buildmode=plugin Loads the built .so file into memory Notes Plugins are rebuilt each time Soulsolid starts (no caching) Only the default branch is cloned (no branch/tag/commit support) Repository must contain a go.mod file at the root Building arbitrary code carries inherent security risks (same as loading pre-built .so files) Best Practices Error handling: Return meaningful errors from all methods. Logging: Use the standard log/slog package for logging. Configuration validation: Validate required configuration in NewDownloader. Progress callbacks: Implement progress callbacks for downloads to provide user feedback. Status reporting: Return appropriate status information in GetStatus(). Thread safety: Ensure your downloader is safe for concurrent use. Example Plugin There’s a dummy plugin I have created to serve as an example. You can find it here.
Testing Test your plugin by:
Building it with go build -buildmode=plugin Adding it to your Soulsolid config Restarting Soulsolid Testing the downloader through the web interface Troubleshooting Plugin not loading: Check that the path is correct and the file is readable. Symbol not found: Ensure you export NewDownloader (capital N). Configuration errors: Check that required config keys are provided. Version mismatches: Rebuild the plugin when updating Soulsolid.
summary: This guide is for developers who want to write a downloader plugin for Soulsolid in Go. If you just want to use an existing plugin, see Downloading instead; no code needed.
title: Plugins

The analyze feature runs an analysis of the metadata of your library and fills in the missing gaps.
Analyze Jobs Each analysis runs as a background job and can be started from the Analyze section of the web UI.
AcoustID Analysis The AcoustID analysis job computes acoustic fingerprints for your audio tracks and matches them against the AcoustID database. This helps identify songs accurately, filling in missing or incorrect metadata such as track titles, artists, albums, and other tags. It’s particularly useful for tracks with incomplete information or those obtained from unknown sources.
Lyrics Analysis The Lyrics analysis job searches for and adds lyrics to your tracks using configured providers. Currently supported providers include:
Lrclib: A lyrics database that provides synchronized (LRC timestamped) and plain text lyrics. The job attempts to fetch lyrics for all tracks. For tracks that already have lyrics, you can control the behavior with two options available in the UI:
Skip existing: skip tracks that already have lyrics entirely Override without queuing: apply new lyrics immediately if they differ, without a manual review step If neither option is set, tracks with differing existing lyrics are sent to the lyrics queue for manual review. See the Lyrics docs for queue type details.
File Paths (Reorganize) Applies the current path templates to every track in the library and moves files to match. See Reorganize Library.
Merge Finds artists, albums and genres that are the same but spelled differently (for example Hip-Hop and Hip Hop) and lets you merge them into one. It also finds duplicate tracks (the same recording stored in more than one file) using AcoustID. See Merge.
Job Logs This is how the job logs look. You can browse these logs and see which tracks were processed correctly and which failed. Failed tracks have a manual_fix="track" link: click it to open the track in the tag editor and fix it by hand.
time=2025-11-30T11:42:34.416+01:00 level=INFO msg="Starting job" name="Analyze Lyrics for Library" time=2025-11-30T11:42:34.416+01:00 level=INFO msg="EXECUTE STARTED: Lyrics job task is running" color=pink time=2025-11-30T11:42:34.416+01:00 level=INFO msg="Enabled lyrics providers" providers="map[dummy:true lrclib:true]" color=blue time=2025-11-30T11:42:34.416+01:00 level=INFO msg="Starting lyrics analysis" totalTracks=16 color=blue time=2025-11-30T11:42:34.416+01:00 level=INFO msg=Progress percentage=0 status="Starting analysis of 16 tracks" time=2025-11-30T11:42:34.424+01:00 level=INFO msg=Progress percentage=0 status="Processing track 1/16: 4 + 20" time=2025-11-30T11:42:34.424+01:00 level=INFO msg="Skipping track with existing lyrics" trackID=5a56532c-9f5b-57d0-a9eb-c7e6f81cac77 title="4 + 20" lyricsLength=661 color=orange time=2025-11-30T11:42:36.890+01:00 level=ERROR msg="Failed to add lyrics for track" trackID=c3fded61-1a6b-5fbb-ac51-ce1ec30ae07c title="A contraluz" provider=lrclib error="failed to search lyrics with provider 'lrclib': no lyrics found" manual_fix="track" time=2025-11-30T11:42:36.890+01:00 level=INFO msg=Progress percentage=6 status="Processing track 2/16: Almost Cut My Hair" time=2025-11-30T11:42:38.569+01:00 level=INFO msg="Lyrics analysis completed" totalTracks=16 processed=2 updated=0 skipped=14 color=green

Analyze Jobs

Each analysis runs as a background job and can be started from the Analyze section of the web UI.

Reorganize moves the files already in your library so they match your current path templates. When you change how folders and files are named, or fix the tags of a bunch of tracks, the files on disk are still in their old place. Reorganize works out where each track should be and moves it there.
What you can do Move every misplaced file to the location your path templates give it. Optionally make every path FAT32-safe, for syncing to SD cards, USB sticks and similar devices. See your current path templates, with a link to change them in Settings. Running a reorganize Go to Analyze → File Paths and start the job. It runs in the background as a job, so you can follow its progress and cancel it from the Jobs section.
For each track in your library, Soulsolid:
Works out where the file should be, using your current path templates and the track’s tags. Skips the track if it’s already in the right place, or if its file is missing from disk. Otherwise moves the file to its new location, creating folders as needed, and updates the library to point to it. Folders left empty after files are moved out are removed. A track that can’t be moved never stops the job: it’s counted as an error and logged, and the job carries on. When it finishes, the job reports how many files were moved, skipped and failed.
Reorganize moves files on disk. If other programs (a media server, a sync tool) point at the old locations, they’ll need to rescan afterwards. A webhook can do this for you.
When to use it After changing your path templates in Settings. After correcting tags on many tracks, for example after fixing an artist’s name or merging duplicate artists or albums. Merging doesn’t move files, so run a reorganize afterwards. FAT32-safe filenames Check FAT32-safe filenames before starting the job to also clean every path so it works on FAT32 drives:
Everything is lowercased. Characters FAT32 doesn’t allow (: * ? " < > | \) are replaced with -. Trailing dots and spaces are removed. Overly long names are shortened. If two tracks would end up at the same path, a number is added to the second one (_1, _2, …) so neither is lost. This checkbox applies only to that run. To have every import use FAT32-safe paths too, enable FAT32-safe filenames in Settings. See Paths → FAT32 Safe Mode for details.
Configuration Reorganize has no settings of its own. It uses the same path templates as importing, under import.paths. See Paths for the template syntax.
Related Paths: the path template syntax. Importing: uses the same templates when files first arrive. Merge: run a reorganize after merging. Jobs: follow and cancel the reorganize job.
summary: Reorganize moves the files already in your library so they match your current path templates. When you change how folders and files are named, or fix the tags of a bunch of tracks, the files on disk are still in their old place. Reorganize works out where each track should be and moves it there.
title: Reorganize

content:
Soulsolid can find lyrics for your tracks and embed them in the audio files, using lyrics providers. Lyrics providers are separate from downloader plugins, so you get lyrics no matter where your music came from.
For how to fetch lyrics and review them in the app, see Lyrics.
Lyric Providers A lyrics provider looks up lyrics for a track using its tags (title, artist, album). Currently LRCLIB is supported.
Providers may supply:
Unsynced lyrics: plain text lyrics Synced lyrics: lyrics with timestamps for each line (LRC format), which some players use to scroll along with the song Configuration Lyrics providers are configured in config.yaml:
lyrics: providers: lrclib: enabled: true prefer_synced: falseProvider Options enabled: Enables or disables the provider entirely. prefer_synced: When true, synced (timestamped) lyrics are used instead of plain lyrics when both are available. Some players, like Navidrome, need synced lyrics. Lyrics Analysis Job The lyrics analysis job runs through all tracks in the library and attempts to fetch lyrics for each one. It can be started from the web UI under Analyze → Lyrics.
Options Option Default Description Provider — Which provider to use (e.g. LRCLIB) Skip tracks that already have lyrics on Only look up tracks that don’t have lyrics yet Override without queuing off Replace existing lyrics straight away, without sending them to the queue for review Behavior Tracks with no lyrics: lyrics are fetched and embedded directly. Tracks marked as instrumental: skipped. Tracks with existing lyrics (when not skipped): by default, if the new lyrics differ, the track goes to the queue for review; with Override without queuing, the existing lyrics are replaced. Lyrics Queue When the analysis finds tracks that need your decision, they’re placed in the lyrics queue. The queue is kept in memory, so it’s emptied when Soulsolid restarts.
Queue Types Type Trigger Available Actions Existing lyrics Track already has lyrics and the new lyrics differ Override (use the new lyrics), Edit Manually Not found Provider has no lyrics for the track No Lyrics (mark the track as instrumental), Edit Manually Failed Provider search returned an error Skip, No Lyrics, Edit Manually
summary: Soulsolid can find lyrics for your tracks and embed them in the audio files, using lyrics providers. Lyrics providers are separate from downloader plugins, so you get lyrics no matter where your music came from.

Over time a library collects the same artist, album or genre spelled in slightly different ways: Hip-Hop, Hip Hop and hiphop, or Un Verano Sin Tí and un verano sin ti. It also collects the same song stored twice, say a FLAC and an MP3 of the same recording. The Merge section finds these and lets you clean them up.
What you can do Find artists, albums and genres that are the same but spelled differently, and merge them into one. Find duplicate tracks (the same recording in more than one file) and delete the copies you don’t want. Mark a group of duplicate tracks as intentional, so it stops showing up. Open it from Merge in the sidebar (under Analyze).
Artists, albums and genres Click Scan on the Artists, Albums or Genres card. Soulsolid groups names that only differ by case, punctuation, accents or spacing. Albums are only grouped when their artist matches too, so two different albums that share a title aren’t mixed up.
For each group:
Pick the name to keep with the radio button. Soulsolid suggests the best-looking one (proper capitalization over ALL CAPS or all lowercase). Untick any variant you don’t want merged. Click Merge. The merge runs as a job. Every track that used one of the other spellings is moved over to the name you kept, and its audio file tags are updated too, so the fix sticks even outside Soulsolid.
File paths aren’t updated after a merge. If your folder names include the artist, album or genre, run Reorganize afterwards to move the files to their new folders.
Duplicate tracks Duplicate tracks are found by AcoustID: two files with the same AcoustID are the same recording, even if they’re in different formats, bitrates or have slightly different tags. So run an AcoustID analysis first; tracks without an AcoustID can’t be matched.
Why not on import? When importing, Soulsolid compares the audio fingerprints directly, which already catches most duplicates without depending on an online service. But small differences (another encoding, bitrate, a slight edit, noise) can make two fingerprints of the same song differ slightly. AcoustID, a crowdsourced ID for each recording, catches those.
Click Scan on the Tracks card. For each group of duplicates you have two choices:
Delete selected: tick the files you want to get rid of and click it. The ticked files are permanently deleted from disk and removed from the library. Playlists that contained a deleted copy now point to the copy you kept. Keep: leaves every file where it is and records the group as intentional duplicates, so it stops showing up in future scans. Nothing on disk changes. Marked a group as Keep by mistake? Tick Include kept before scanning to see those groups again.
Related Metadata / Tagging: run an AcoustID analysis before looking for duplicate tracks. Reorganize: move files to match their merged names. Importing: how duplicates are handled when music first arrives. Jobs: follow merge jobs.

Long-running tasks like imports, downloads and analyses run in the background as jobs. The jobs section configures their log files and webhooks. Jobs themselves are kept in memory (the list is emptied on restart), while their logs are saved as files, by default in ./logs/jobs.
For following, cancelling and reading jobs in the app, and how webhooks work in detail, see Jobs.
Here’s an example configuration:
jobs: log: true log_path: ./logs/jobs webhooks: enabled: true job_trigger: - directory_import - download_album command: | # ntfy curl -d "Backup successful 😀" ntfy.sh/mytopiclog: Enable or disable job logging. log_path: The directory where job logs are stored. webhooks: Configuration for sending notifications about job status. enabled: Enable or disable webhooks. job_trigger: List of job types to send notifications for ("*" = all). Formerly job_types, which is still read but deprecated. command: Shell command run when a matching job finishes. It runs in the background and is stopped after 30 seconds. It can use these placeholders: {{.Name}}, {{.Type}}, {{.Status}}, {{.Message}}, {{.Duration}}. See Webhooks for how they’re filled in safely and how to pass secrets. Job Scheduling Only one job runs at a time. Additional jobs wait in line and start automatically when the current job finishes. Webhooks are the exception: they start right away.
Job Types Type Triggered by directory_import Importing a directory of audio files calculate_metrics Recalculating the library metrics shown on the dashboard download_track Downloading a single track via a plugin download_album Downloading a full album via a plugin download_artist Downloading all albums for an artist via a plugin download_tracks Downloading multiple tracks in bulk download_playlist Downloading a playlist via a plugin analyze_acoustid Running AcoustID fingerprint analysis on the library analyze_lyrics Running lyrics analysis on the library analyze_reorganize Reorganizing library file paths analyze_merge Merging artists, albums, genres or tracks webhook A webhook command run after another job Notification Examples Telegram Sends a Telegram message with job details:
jobs: webhooks: enabled: true job_trigger: - directory_import - download_album command: | TEXT="🎵 Job {{.Name}} ({{.Type}}) {{.Status}}\n📝 {{.Message}}\n⏱️ Duration: {{.Duration}}" && \ curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d "{\"chat_id\": \"<chat_id>\", \"text\": \"$TEXT\", \"parse_mode\": \"HTML\"}" \ https://api.telegram.org/bot<bot_token>/sendMessagentfy Sends a notification to an ntfy.sh topic for every job:
jobs: webhooks: enabled: true job_trigger: - "*" command: curl -d "Job {{.Name}} {{.Status}} 😀" ntfy.sh/mytopicEmby Triggers a library rescan in Emby after imports:
jobs: webhooks: enabled: true job_trigger: - directory_import command: curl -X POST 'http://localhost:8096/Emby/Library/Refresh?api_key=your_emby_api_key'

Playlists let you group tracks from your library into named, ordered lists and export them as standard .m3u files that other players and devices can open.
What you can do Create a playlist with a name and an optional description. Add a single track, a whole album, or every track by an artist. Remove tracks from a playlist. Rename, edit the description of, or delete a playlist. Export a playlist as an .m3u file. Creating a playlist In the Playlists section, click to create a new playlist, give it a name and, optionally, a description.
Adding music From the Library, use the Add to Playlist button on any track, album or artist and pick the playlist.
Adding a track adds just that track. Adding an album adds every track on it. Adding an artist adds every track by that artist. Tracks that are already in the playlist are skipped, so adding an album twice won’t duplicate anything.
Managing a playlist Open a playlist to see its tracks with their title, artist and duration, and the total duration of the playlist. From there you can remove tracks, edit the name and description, or delete the playlist.
Deleting a playlist doesn’t delete any music: the tracks stay in your library.
Exporting to M3U Export downloads the playlist as <playlist name>.m3u. The file lists each track in playlist order with its duration, artist and title, followed by the full path to the audio file on disk.
Because the file uses full paths, it works best with players that see your music at the same location as Soulsolid, such as a media server reading the same library folder.
Configuration Playlists have no settings. They’re stored in the library database, so they’re included when you back up the database.
Related Library: where you add tracks, albums and artists to playlists. Streaming: play your tracks in the browser. Downloading: download playlists from a music service.

Soulsolid has a built-in audio player so you can listen to a track right in the browser while you browse, tag or review your music. It’s there to help you check what you’re looking at (is this the right version? is the file broken?) rather than to be a full music player.

content:
Anything in Soulsolid that can take a while (importing a folder, downloading an album, running a lyrics analysis, reorganizing files, refreshing metrics) runs as a background job. You can keep using the app while it runs, follow its progress, read its log, and cancel it. Soulsolid can also run a webhook command when a job finishes, for example to send you a notification or tell your media server to rescan.
What you can do Follow every job’s progress and status in the All Jobs section. Read the log of any job, live while it runs. Cancel a running or waiting job. Clear finished jobs from the list. Run a webhook command when certain jobs finish. How jobs run Only one job runs at a time. If you start a job while another is running, it waits in line and starts automatically when the current one finishes, oldest first. This keeps jobs from getting in each other’s way, for example an import reading files that a download is still writing.
Each job has a status:
Status Meaning Pending Waiting for the running job to finish. Running In progress, with a progress bar and a message saying what it’s doing. Completed Finished. Some jobs (like imports) can complete with errors when only some items failed. Failed Stopped because of an error. Cancelled You cancelled it. Jobs are kept in memory, so the jobs list is emptied when Soulsolid restarts. Their log files stay on disk.
Job logs When job logging is enabled (jobs.log: true), every job writes its own log file in jobs.log_path, named after the date and the job. You can read it from the job’s card in the app:
inline, refreshed live while the job runs, full screen, with colors, raw, as plain text. Logs are color-coded so errors (red) and warnings (yellow) stand out. When a job fails on a specific track, the log line includes a link to open that track in the tag editor and fix it by hand. See Analyze → Job Logs for an example.
Cancelling and clearing Cancel stops a running job as soon as it safely can (usually after the current track), or removes a pending one from the line. Clear Finished Jobs removes every completed, failed and cancelled job from the list, and deletes their log files. Webhooks A webhook is a shell command Soulsolid runs when a job finishes. Use it to send a notification (ntfy, Telegram, Discord…), trigger a media server rescan, start a backup, or anything else you can do from a shell. See Jobs configuration for how to set it up and ready-to-use examples.
Webhooks are configured with:
job_trigger: which job types trigger the command ("*" for all). command: the command to run. It can use these placeholders: Placeholder Value {{.Name}} The job’s name, e.g. Download Album or Download Playlist: Road trip {{.Type}} The job type, e.g. download_album {{.Status}} completed, failed or cancelled {{.Message}} The job’s final message {{.Duration}} How long the job took You can also use simple conditions, such as {{if eq .Status "failed"}}...{{end}} or {{or .Message "no message"}}.
How webhook commands run Each webhook shows up in the jobs list as its own job, named Webhook: <job name>, so you can check that it worked:
The command runs with /bin/sh. What it prints is saved in the webhook job’s log (when job logging is enabled). If the command exits with an error, or takes longer than 30 seconds, the webhook job fails. Cancel stops the command and everything it started. Nothing the command starts keeps running after it finishes, including background processes (curl ... &). Webhooks don’t wait in line: they start right away, even while another job runs, so notifications aren’t delayed. Webhook jobs never trigger webhooks themselves, even with job_trigger: ["*"]. Passing secrets to webhooks For safety, a webhook command does not see Soulsolid’s environment variables, so API keys you’ve given Soulsolid can’t leak into it. It only sees:
PATH, so commands like curl can be found. Variables whose name starts with SOULSOLID_WEBHOOK_, passed through as they are. The job’s values as SOULSOLID_JOB_NAME, SOULSOLID_JOB_TYPE, SOULSOLID_JOB_STATUS, SOULSOLID_JOB_MESSAGE and SOULSOLID_JOB_DURATION. Put tokens and URLs in SOULSOLID_WEBHOOK_* variables so they never appear in config.yaml or in logs:
command: curl -s -d "{{.Name}} {{.Status}}" "https://ntfy.sh/$SOULSOLID_WEBHOOK_NTFY_TOPIC"Anything else the command needs, such as HOME or SSL_CERT_FILE, has to be passed the same way and exported in the command, e.g. export SSL_CERT_FILE="$SOULSOLID_WEBHOOK_SSL_CERT_FILE"; curl ....
Track titles and names are safe Job names and messages can contain text that comes from your files, like track titles or playlist names. Soulsolid makes sure that text is always treated as plain text: each placeholder becomes exactly one argument of the command, however it’s quoted. A track titled "; rm -rf ~; " is just a title, not a command.
There’s one thing to watch out for: if your command hands a value to another shell (sh -c, bash -c, ssh host '...', su -c, eval), that shell will run it as code. Pass the value as an argument instead, or read the variable inside:
command: sh -c 'notify "$1"' _ {{.Name}} # value as an argument command: sh -c 'notify "$SOULSOLID_JOB_NAME"' # the inner shell reads the variableTo keep things safe, a webhook doesn’t run if its command:
uses a placeholder inside $(...), backticks, heredocs or $'...', or anywhere after one of these (use the SOULSOLID_JOB_* variables there instead); formats a value with printf, urlquery, html, js or slice (do that formatting in the command itself, for example with jq). Sending JSON Placeholders are inserted as they are, so a " or \ in a track title can break a JSON body written by hand, such as -d '{"text": "{{.Name}}"}'. That can’t run anything, but the service you’re calling may reject the request. To always send valid JSON, build it with jq (it must be installed where Soulsolid runs) and pipe it to curl:
command: >- jq -n --arg name "{{.Name}}" --arg status "{{.Status}}" '{text: "\($name) \($status)"}' | curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @- https://example.com/hookConfiguration jobs: log: true # write a log file for every job log_path: /app/logs/jobs # where log files are written webhooks: enabled: false # run a command when a job finishes job_trigger: ["*"] # which job types trigger it ("*" = all) command: 'curl -d "{{.Name}} {{.Status}}" ntfy.sh/mytopic'When log is off, jobs still run but no logs are kept.
Related Jobs configuration: job types and webhook examples. Importing, Downloading, Lyrics, Reorganize, Merge, Metadata, Metrics: everything that runs as a job.
