All of Soulsolid’s settings live in a single config.yaml file. You can edit that file directly, or change most settings from the Settings page in the app. This page explains how the Settings page works; for every option in the file, see the Configuration reference.
What you can do Change settings from the app, without touching the config file. View your current config.yaml. Download a backup of your library database. First start If there’s no config file when Soulsolid starts, it creates one with sensible defaults, so you can run it without any setup. It also creates your library and download folders if they don’t exist yet.
If the config file has a mistake (for example a required setting is missing, or it refers to an environment variable that isn’t set), Soulsolid won’t start and tells you what’s wrong.
The Settings page The Settings page lets you change:
your download folder, import options: move or copy, duplicate handling, always queue, allow missing metadata, FAT32-safe filenames, your path templates (see Paths), metadata providers: turn them on or off and set their API keys, logging and job logging. Changes take effect right away and are saved to config.yaml.
Some settings are read-only in the app and can only be changed in the config file (they’re marked as such on the page). These are the ones that only apply when Soulsolid starts, or that are risky to change while it’s running:
the library folder, the database location, downloader plugins and artwork settings, lyrics providers, the server port, whether the download folder watcher starts automatically, webhooks. Edit config.yaml and restart Soulsolid to change them.
Running Soulsolid with a read-only config file (common with containers and Kubernetes ConfigMaps)? Changes made on the Settings page still apply until the next restart, but can’t be saved to the file. Soulsolid logs a warning when this happens.
Keeping secrets out of the config file API keys and tokens don’t have to be written in config.yaml. You can have Soulsolid read them from an environment variable (!env_var) or from a file (!env_file, handy for Docker and Kubernetes secrets):
metadata: providers: discogs: secret: !env_var DISCOGS_API_KEY acoustid: secret: !env_file ACOUSTID_CLIENT_KEY_FILE # ACOUSTID_CLIENT_KEY_FILE=/run/secrets/acoustidSee Configuration → Environment Variables.
Backing up the database The Settings page has a button to download your library database. It contains everything Soulsolid knows about your library: tracks, artists, albums, playlists and tags.
The backup only includes the database, not your music files. Back up your library folder separately.
Related Configuration reference: every option in config.yaml. Importing, Paths, Lyrics, Jobs: settings for each feature. Self hosted: where the config file lives in a container.

Soulsolid is a web app: a single server that serves the interface you use in your browser and an API you can call from scripts. This page covers the server side of running it. For installing Soulsolid with Podman, Docker, Compose or Kubernetes, see Self hosted.
The web interface By default Soulsolid listens on port 3535. Open http://<your-server>:3535 in a browser to use it. To use a different port, set server.port in the config and restart.
Soulsolid has no built-in login. Anyone who can reach the port can use the app, including deleting music. If it’s reachable from outside your home network, put it behind a reverse proxy with authentication (or a VPN).
Health check GET /health answers OK while the server is running. Use it for container health checks, Kubernetes liveness probes or uptime monitoring:
livenessProbe: httpGet: path: /health port: 3535Using Soulsolid from scripts Every action you can take in the interface can also be done over HTTP. When a request doesn’t come from the web interface, Soulsolid answers with JSON instead of a web page, so you can use curl or your own scripts to search the library, start imports, check jobs and more. See the API reference.
Configuration server: port: 3535 # the port the web interface listens on show_routes: false # print every API route to the log on startupBoth settings only apply on startup, so restart Soulsolid after changing them.
Related Self hosted: running Soulsolid in a container. API reference: every route and what it returns. Logging: the server’s own logs.

Soulsolid runs in your browser. Once it’s running, open http://<your-server>:3535 and you land on the Dashboard.
The dashboard The dashboard is the app’s home page. It shows:
Library overview: how many tracks, artists and albums you have. Charts about your collection: release years, genres, formats and how complete your tags are (see Metrics). Use Refresh Metrics to update them. Quick Actions: shortcuts to Import Music and Browse Library. Recent Jobs: the latest background jobs and how they went. Finding your way around The sidebar takes you to every part of the app:
Section What it’s for Dashboard Overview and charts. Library Browse, search and manage your music (Library). Playlists Your playlists (Playlists). Importing Import folders and review the import queue (Importing). Downloaders One entry per downloader plugin you’ve configured (Downloading). Analyze Library-wide jobs: Metadata (AcoustID), Lyrics, File Paths and Merge. See Analyze. All Jobs Everything running in the background (Jobs). Settings Change your configuration (Configuration). Badges in the sidebar show how many tracks you have, how many are waiting in the import and lyrics queues, and how many jobs are running.
Every page has its own address, so you can bookmark a section or share a link to a specific track’s tag editor.

Soulsolid writes a log of what it’s doing (starting up, requests, errors) to the console. It’s the first place to look when something doesn’t work as expected.
These are the application logs. Each background job also writes its own log, which you can read from the app; see Jobs → Job logs.
Where to find the logs Logs are written to the standard output of the process:
Container: podman logs soulsolid or docker logs soulsolid (add -f to follow them live). Kubernetes: kubectl logs <pod>. Running it directly: in the terminal where you started it. Each line shows the time, the level, where it came from, and the message.
Log levels Level What you see info (default) Normal activity, warnings and errors. Good for everyday use. debug Much more detail, including every request made by the web interface. Use it when investigating a problem or reporting a bug. Log formats Format Looks like Use it for logfmt (default) key=value pairs Reading in a terminal, and most log tools. text Plain, human-readable text Reading in a terminal. json One JSON object per line Sending logs to a log collector (Loki, Elasticsearch, …). Configuration logger: enabled: true # turn logging on or off level: info # info or debug format: logfmt # logfmt, text or json htmx_debug: false # extra debugging information in the web interface, for troubleshootingThese can also be changed from the Settings page.
Related Jobs: per-job logs, readable from the app. Configuration: the Settings page.

Importing: Import music from directories with automatic fingerprinting Metadata Tagging: Auto-tag using MusicBrainz and Discogs APIs Telegram Integration: Control via Telegram bot Web UI: Mobile-friendly interface for all operations Job Management: Background processing for downloads, imports, and syncs Screenshots Main dashboard interface
Library browsing and organization
App configuration options
Quick Start 🦭 Container Usage The application can run without copying config.yaml into the container. If no config file exists, it will automatically create one with sensible defaults.
Environment Variable Support Soulsolid supports environment variables in configuration files using the !env_var tag:
telegram: token: !env_var TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN metadata: providers: discogs: secret: !env_var DISCOGS_API_KEYThe application will fail to start if a referenced environment variable is not set.
# Build the image podman build -t soulsolid . # Run with environment variables podman run -d \ --name soulsolid \ -p 3535:3535 \ -v /host/music:/app/library \ -v /host/downloads:/app/downloads \ -v /host/logs:/app/logs \ # optional -v /host/library.db:/data/library.db \ -v /host/config.yaml:/config/config.yaml \ soulsolidOptionally, to hide secrets, you can use !env_var syntax anywhere in your config.yaml:
telegram: token: !env_var TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN metadata: providers: discogs: secret: !env_var DISCOGS_API_KEYThe web interface will be available at http://localhost:3535.
